156	# Lexical appendix
157	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
158	#
159	# The rules above are written over tokens. This appendix defines those tokens,
160	# so a consumer can build the token stream the rules consume.
161	#
162	# Keywords are matched before identifiers. Each is its own terminal, spelled in
163	# upper case after the keyword itself: `use` is USE, `fn` is FN, and so on for
164	# async, await, spawn, parallel, gpu, frame, if, unless, else, match, default,
165	# return, while, until, do, for, forall, forever, in, let, var, const, or, and,
166	# not, true, false, None, from, as, break, continue, extends, is, includes,
167	# implements, type, enum, struct, class, trait, super, public, protected,
168	# shared, private, system, local, abstract, must_use, out, runtime, intrinsic.
169	#
170	# Note that `system`, `gpu`, `frame`, `local`, `default` and `out` are keywords
171	# that also appear where a name is expected, which is why several rules above
172	# accept them in name position.
173	#
174	# Punctuation terminals, longest match first within each group:
175	#   AT @              SEMICOLON ;        COLON :          DOUBLE_COLON ::
176	#   FAT_ARROW =>      ARROW ->           LEFT_ARROW <-
177	#   EQUAL ==          NOT_EQUAL !=       LESS_THAN_EQUAL <=
178	#   GREATER_THAN_EQUAL >=                LESS_THAN <       GREATER_THAN >
179	#   ASSIGN =          ASSIGN_ADD +=      ASSIGN_SUB -=     ASSIGN_MUL *=
180	#   ASSIGN_DIV /=     ASSIGN_MOD %=
181	#   PLUS +            INCREMENT ++       MINUS -           DECREMENT --
182	#   STAR *            SLASH /            PERCENT %         COMMA ,
183	#   RANGE ..          RANGE_INCLUSIVE ..=                  DOT .
184	#   L_PAREN (         R_PAREN )          L_BRACKET [       R_BRACKET ]
185	#   L_BRACE {         R_BRACE }          PIPE |            AMPERSAND &
186	#   CARET ^           QUESTION_MARK ?    QUESTION_QUESTION ??           TILDE ~
187	#
188	# Literal terminals:
189	#   IDENT    [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*
190	#   INT      [0-9]+(_[0-9]+)*
191	#   FLOAT    [0-9]+(_[0-9]+)*\.[0-9]+(_[0-9]+)*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?
192	#            or  \.[0-9]+(_[0-9]+)*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?
193	#   BINARY   0[bB][01_]+
194	#   HEX      0[xX][0-9a-fA-F_]+
195	#   OCTAL    0[oO][0-7_]+
196	#   STRING   '...' or "..." with backslash escapes
197	#   REGEX    re'...' or re"..." followed by any of the flags [igmsu]
198	#   FSTRING_START / FSTRING_MID / FSTRING_END
199	#            an f-string is split around its interpolations: f"a{x}b{y}c"
200	#            lexes as FSTRING_START, the tokens of x, FSTRING_MID, the tokens of
201	#            y, then FSTRING_END.
202	#
203	# Because FLOAT admits a leading dot, a tuple field access lexes as an identifier
204	# followed by a FLOAT: `t.0` is IDENT FLOAT, not IDENT DOT INT. The rules above
205	# model that directly, in `tuple_field`.
206	#
207	# Discarded by the lexer, never present in the stream: horizontal whitespace,
208	# `//` line comments, `/* */` block comments (which nest), a leading `#!` line,
209	# and a byte-order mark.
210	#
211	# Indentation. The lexer converts line structure into three synthetic terminals,
212	# maintaining a stack of indentation columns that starts holding only column 0:
213	#
214	#   1. At each newline outside any bracket, measure the next non-blank,
215	#      non-comment line's indentation.
216	#   2. Greater than the top of the stack: push it and emit INDENT.
217	#   3. Less than the top: pop and emit DEDENT until the top matches. If no entry
218	#      matches, the indentation is inconsistent and the input is rejected.
219	#   4. Equal to the top: emit STMT_END, ending the logical line.
220	#   5. At end of input, emit a DEDENT for every column left above 0.
221	#
222	# A newline inside (), [] or {} continues the logical line and produces nothing.
223	# STMT_END is emitted before INDENT, so a block header reads as
224	# `header STMT_END INDENT ... DEDENT`, and no STMT_END follows a DEDENT.
225	#
226	# Longest match resolves every overlapping operator before the grammar sees the
227	# stream, so `..=` never lexes as `..` then `=`, and the same holds for `..`/`.`,
228	# `::`/`:`, `??`/`?`, `++`/`+` and `--`/`-`. None of these is an ordered-choice
229	# hazard in the rules above.
230	#
231	# Associativity. Precedence is expressed by the layering of the expression rules,
232	# but a rule of the form `a <- b (op b)*` yields a flat sequence and records no
233	# associativity at all. A consumer folding that sequence into a tree must apply:
234	#
235	#   left       * / %  + - ^  << >>  &  |  == !=  < > <= >=  and  or
236	#   right      = += -= *= /= %=   and the ?: conditional
237	#   non        .. ..=      (a range does not chain)
238	#
239	# Unary operators bind tighter than any binary operator, and postfix operators —
240	# call, index, member access, `as`, `?` — bind tighter still.
241

# version: 3

# The Miri language grammar, over the token stream the lexer produces.
#
# Terminals are token names; the lexical appendix at the end of this file gives
# each one's pattern and the indentation algorithm that synthesises INDENT,
# DEDENT and STMT_END. A consumer implements that lexer, then these rules.
#
# This grammar is an OVER-APPROXIMATION. It accepts token sequences the
# compiler rejects, so it is suitable for validation and for constrained
# decoding, but it is not a substitute for the compiler. It does not express:
#   - the parser's recursion depth limit (MAX_PARSE_DEPTH = 256)
#   - contextual keywords, whose meaning depends on surrounding tokens
#   - lookahead-driven disambiguation, such as telling a generic argument list
#     from a chain of comparisons: `List<int` is accepted here as the comparison
#     `List < int`, while the compiler reads the same tokens as an unterminated
#     generic argument list and rejects them
#   - rejection of duplicate match branches
#   - name resolution, type checking, and every other semantic rule
#
# Precedence is expressed by the layering of the expression rules. Associativity
# is NOT expressible in PEG structure: a rule of the form `a <- b (op b)*`
# yields a flat sequence, and a consumer building a tree must apply the
# associativity table in the appendix.

program <- statement*

statement <- declaration / compound_statement / simple_statement

block <- STMT_END INDENT statement+ DEDENT
body <- COLON (block / statement) / block

declaration <- attribute* modifier* declaration_kind
attribute <- AT attribute_name (L_PAREN argument_list? R_PAREN)? STMT_END?
attribute_name <- IDENT / MUST_USE / DEFAULT / OUT / SHARED / LOCAL
modifier <- PUBLIC / PRIVATE / PROTECTED / SHARED / ABSTRACT / ASYNC / MUST_USE / INTRINSIC / RUNTIME STRING? / contextual_static
contextual_static <- &(IDENT FN) IDENT
declaration_kind <- use_declaration / function_declaration / class_declaration / struct_declaration / enum_declaration / trait_declaration / type_declaration

use_declaration <- USE use_path (AS IDENT)? STMT_END
use_path <- use_segment (DOT use_segment)* (DOT use_group)?
use_group <- L_BRACE use_segment (COMMA use_segment)* R_BRACE
use_segment <- IDENT / SYSTEM / GPU / LOCAL / TYPE / DEFAULT

function_declaration <- FN function_name generic_parameters? L_PAREN parameter_list? R_PAREN type_expression? function_tail
function_name <- IDENT / DEFAULT
function_tail <- body / STMT_END
parameter_list <- parameter (COMMA parameter)* COMMA?
parameter <- OUT? IDENT OUT? type_expression? (ASSIGN expression)?

class_declaration <- CLASS IDENT generic_parameters? extends_clause? implements_clause? member_block
struct_declaration <- STRUCT IDENT generic_parameters? extends_clause? implements_clause? member_block
trait_declaration <- TRAIT IDENT generic_parameters? extends_clause? member_block
enum_declaration <- ENUM IDENT generic_parameters? implements_clause? enum_block
extends_clause <- EXTENDS type_expression (COMMA type_expression)*
implements_clause <- IMPLEMENTS type_expression (COMMA type_expression)*
member_block <- STMT_END INDENT member+ DEDENT
member <- declaration / field_declaration
field_declaration <- attribute* modifier* (LET / VAR / CONST) IDENT type_expression? (ASSIGN expression)? STMT_END / attribute* modifier* IDENT type_expression (ASSIGN expression)? STMT_END
shared_declaration <- SHARED IDENT type_expression? (ASSIGN expression)? STMT_END
enum_block <- STMT_END INDENT enum_member+ DEDENT
enum_member <- declaration / enum_variant
enum_variant <- IDENT (L_PAREN type_expression (COMMA type_expression)* R_PAREN)? STMT_END

type_declaration <- TYPE IDENT generic_parameters? (IS type_set / (EXTENDS / IMPLEMENTS / INCLUDES) type_expression) STMT_END

compound_statement <- if_statement / unless_statement / while_statement / until_statement / do_statement / for_statement / forall_statement / match_statement / gpu_statement / forever_statement

if_statement <- IF expression body else_clause?
unless_statement <- UNLESS expression body else_clause?
else_clause <- ELSE (if_statement / body)
while_statement <- WHILE expression body
until_statement <- UNTIL expression body
forever_statement <- FOREVER body
do_statement <- DO body (WHILE / UNTIL) expression STMT_END
for_statement <- FOR iteration_clause body
forall_statement <- FORALL iteration_clause body
iteration_clause <- loop_variables IN expression (COMMA expression)*
loop_variables <- loop_variable (COMMA loop_variable)*
loop_variable <- IDENT / L_PAREN loop_variables R_PAREN
match_statement <- MATCH expression (inline_match_branches / STMT_END INDENT match_branch+ DEDENT)
inline_match_branches <- COLON match_branch (COMMA match_branch)*
match_branch <- pattern (PIPE pattern)* match_guard? body
match_guard <- IF expression
pattern <- ELSE / DEFAULT / expression

gpu_statement <- GPU gpu_tail
gpu_tail <- function_declaration / forall_statement / for_statement / frame_block / binding_statement
frame_block <- FRAME body

simple_statement <- shared_declaration / binding_statement / return_statement / break_statement / continue_statement / expression_statement
binding_statement <- binding_head ASSIGN block_valued_expression / binding_head (ASSIGN expression)? guard? STMT_END
binding_head <- attribute* modifier* (LET / VAR / CONST) binding_targets type_expression?
block_valued_expression <- match_statement / if_statement / block_bodied_function
block_bodied_function <- FN L_PAREN parameter_list? R_PAREN type_expression? (COLON block / block)
binding_targets <- binding_target (COMMA binding_target)*
binding_target <- IDENT / OUT / L_PAREN binding_targets R_PAREN
return_statement <- RETURN expression? guard? STMT_END
break_statement <- BREAK expression? guard? STMT_END
continue_statement <- CONTINUE guard? STMT_END
expression_statement <- expression guard? STMT_END
guard <- (IF / UNLESS) expression (ELSE expression)?

expression <- assignment_expression
assignment_expression <- assignment_target assign_operator assignment_expression / conditional_expression
assignment_target <- name_atom generic_arguments? postfix_operator*
assign_operator <- ASSIGN / ASSIGN_ADD / ASSIGN_SUB / ASSIGN_MUL / ASSIGN_DIV / ASSIGN_MOD
conditional_expression <- null_coalescing_expression (QUESTION_MARK expression COLON expression)?
null_coalescing_expression <- logical_or_expression (QUESTION_QUESTION logical_or_expression)*
logical_or_expression <- logical_and_expression ((OR / PIPE) logical_and_expression)*
logical_and_expression <- equality_expression ((AND / AMPERSAND) equality_expression)*
equality_expression <- relational_expression ((EQUAL / NOT_EQUAL) relational_expression)*
relational_expression <- range_expression (relational_operator range_expression)*
relational_operator <- LESS_THAN_EQUAL / GREATER_THAN_EQUAL / LESS_THAN / GREATER_THAN / IS / INCLUDES / IN
range_expression <- additive_expression ((RANGE_INCLUSIVE / RANGE) additive_expression)?
additive_expression <- multiplicative_expression ((PLUS / MINUS / CARET) multiplicative_expression)*
multiplicative_expression <- unary_expression ((STAR / SLASH / PERCENT) unary_expression)*
unary_expression <- unary_operator* postfix_expression
unary_operator <- NOT / MINUS / PLUS / TILDE / INCREMENT / DECREMENT / AWAIT / SPAWN
postfix_expression <- primary_expression postfix_operator*
postfix_operator <- DOT member_name / tuple_field / L_PAREN argument_list? R_PAREN / L_BRACKET expression R_BRACKET / AS type_expression / INCREMENT / DECREMENT / QUESTION_MARK
tuple_field <- FLOAT
member_name <- IDENT / INT / DEFAULT / TYPE / MATCH

primary_expression <- anonymous_function / inline_if_expression / lambda_expression / literal_expression / collection_expression / grouped_expression / identifier_expression / match_statement / if_statement
grouped_expression <- L_PAREN expression (COMMA expression)* R_PAREN
identifier_expression <- qualified_name generic_arguments?
qualified_name <- name_atom
name_atom <- IDENT / OUT / contextual_name
contextual_name <- SUPER / SYSTEM / GPU / FRAME / LOCAL / DEFAULT
collection_expression <- L_BRACKET (expression (COMMA expression)* COMMA?)? R_BRACKET / L_BRACE (map_entry (COMMA map_entry)* COMMA?)? R_BRACE
map_entry <- expression (COLON expression)?
argument_list <- argument (COMMA argument)* COMMA?
argument <- OUT expression / (IDENT COLON)? expression
lambda_expression <- L_PAREN parameter_list? R_PAREN ARROW expression / IDENT ARROW expression
anonymous_function <- FN L_PAREN parameter_list? R_PAREN type_expression? (COLON (block / expression) / block)
inline_if_expression <- IF expression COLON expression (ELSE COLON expression)?

literal_expression <- INT / FLOAT / BINARY / HEX / OCTAL / STRING / REGEX / TRUE / FALSE / NONE / formatted_string
formatted_string <- FSTRING_START expression? (FSTRING_MID expression?)* FSTRING_END

type_expression <- type_union
type_union <- type_postfix ((PIPE / AMPERSAND) type_postfix)*
type_postfix <- type_atom type_suffix*
type_suffix <- QUESTION_MARK / L_BRACKET expression? R_BRACKET
type_atom <- type_name generic_arguments? / L_PAREN type_expression (COMMA type_expression)* R_PAREN / L_BRACKET type_expression (SEMICOLON expression)? R_BRACKET / L_BRACE type_expression (COLON type_expression)? R_BRACE / FN L_PAREN (fn_type_parameter (COMMA fn_type_parameter)*)? R_PAREN type_expression?
type_name <- IDENT / SYSTEM / GPU / FRAME / LOCAL / DEFAULT
generic_arguments <- LESS_THAN generic_argument (COMMA generic_argument)* COMMA? GREATER_THAN
generic_argument <- expression / type_expression
generic_parameters <- LESS_THAN generic_parameter (COMMA generic_parameter)* COMMA? GREATER_THAN
generic_parameter <- IDENT (IS type_set / (EXTENDS / IMPLEMENTS / INCLUDES) type_expression)?
type_set <- type_expression (OR type_expression)*
fn_type_parameter <- IDENT type_expression / type_expression

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Lexical appendix
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The rules above are written over tokens. This appendix defines those tokens,
# so a consumer can build the token stream the rules consume.
#
# Keywords are matched before identifiers. Each is its own terminal, spelled in
# upper case after the keyword itself: `use` is USE, `fn` is FN, and so on for
# async, await, spawn, parallel, gpu, frame, if, unless, else, match, default,
# return, while, until, do, for, forall, forever, in, let, var, const, or, and,
# not, true, false, None, from, as, break, continue, extends, is, includes,
# implements, type, enum, struct, class, trait, super, public, protected,
# shared, private, system, local, abstract, must_use, out, runtime, intrinsic.
#
# Note that `system`, `gpu`, `frame`, `local`, `default` and `out` are keywords
# that also appear where a name is expected, which is why several rules above
# accept them in name position.
#
# Punctuation terminals, longest match first within each group:
#   AT @              SEMICOLON ;        COLON :          DOUBLE_COLON ::
#   FAT_ARROW =>      ARROW ->           LEFT_ARROW <-
#   EQUAL ==          NOT_EQUAL !=       LESS_THAN_EQUAL <=
#   GREATER_THAN_EQUAL >=                LESS_THAN <       GREATER_THAN >
#   ASSIGN =          ASSIGN_ADD +=      ASSIGN_SUB -=     ASSIGN_MUL *=
#   ASSIGN_DIV /=     ASSIGN_MOD %=
#   PLUS +            INCREMENT ++       MINUS -           DECREMENT --
#   STAR *            SLASH /            PERCENT %         COMMA ,
#   RANGE ..          RANGE_INCLUSIVE ..=                  DOT .
#   L_PAREN (         R_PAREN )          L_BRACKET [       R_BRACKET ]
#   L_BRACE {         R_BRACE }          PIPE |            AMPERSAND &
#   CARET ^           QUESTION_MARK ?    QUESTION_QUESTION ??           TILDE ~
#
# Literal terminals:
#   IDENT    [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*
#   INT      [0-9]+(_[0-9]+)*
#   FLOAT    [0-9]+(_[0-9]+)*\.[0-9]+(_[0-9]+)*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?
#            or  \.[0-9]+(_[0-9]+)*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?
#   BINARY   0[bB][01_]+
#   HEX      0[xX][0-9a-fA-F_]+
#   OCTAL    0[oO][0-7_]+
#   STRING   '...' or "..." with backslash escapes
#   REGEX    re'...' or re"..." followed by any of the flags [igmsu]
#   FSTRING_START / FSTRING_MID / FSTRING_END
#            an f-string is split around its interpolations: f"a{x}b{y}c"
#            lexes as FSTRING_START, the tokens of x, FSTRING_MID, the tokens of
#            y, then FSTRING_END.
#
# Because FLOAT admits a leading dot, a tuple field access lexes as an identifier
# followed by a FLOAT: `t.0` is IDENT FLOAT, not IDENT DOT INT. The rules above
# model that directly, in `tuple_field`.
#
# Discarded by the lexer, never present in the stream: horizontal whitespace,
# `//` line comments, `/* */` block comments (which nest), a leading `#!` line,
# and a byte-order mark.
#
# Indentation. The lexer converts line structure into three synthetic terminals,
# maintaining a stack of indentation columns that starts holding only column 0:
#
#   1. At each newline outside any bracket, measure the next non-blank,
#      non-comment line's indentation.
#   2. Greater than the top of the stack: push it and emit INDENT.
#   3. Less than the top: pop and emit DEDENT until the top matches. If no entry
#      matches, the indentation is inconsistent and the input is rejected.
#   4. Equal to the top: emit STMT_END, ending the logical line.
#   5. At end of input, emit a DEDENT for every column left above 0.
#
# A newline inside (), [] or {} continues the logical line and produces nothing.
# STMT_END is emitted before INDENT, so a block header reads as
# `header STMT_END INDENT ... DEDENT`, and no STMT_END follows a DEDENT.
#
# Longest match resolves every overlapping operator before the grammar sees the
# stream, so `..=` never lexes as `..` then `=`, and the same holds for `..`/`.`,
# `::`/`:`, `??`/`?`, `++`/`+` and `--`/`-`. None of these is an ordered-choice
# hazard in the rules above.
#
# Associativity. Precedence is expressed by the layering of the expression rules,
# but a rule of the form `a <- b (op b)*` yields a flat sequence and records no
# associativity at all. A consumer folding that sequence into a tree must apply:
#
#   left       * / %  + - ^  << >>  &  |  == !=  < > <= >=  and  or
#   right      = += -= *= /= %=   and the ?: conditional
#   non        .. ..=      (a range does not chain)
#
# Unary operators bind tighter than any binary operator, and postfix operators —
# call, index, member access, `as`, `?` — bind tighter still.
